summary: Configured node1 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 via nginx with a self-signed certificate that auto-renews before expiry through a systemd timer, reloading nginx gracefully so the service keeps answering requests through cert rotation. Verified automatic renewal in-session (cert serial changed, zero dropped requests) and completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol, confirming persistence and recovery across reboot.
actions_performed: Installed nginx on node1 via apt

Created /etc/nginx/scripts/renew-cert.sh: checks cert expiry with openssl x509 -checkend, regenerates a self-signed 24h cert via openssl req when near expiry, atomically replaces key/cert, validates nginx config, and reloads nginx
Issued the initial self-signed cert into /etc/ssl/rotating/{tls.crt,tls.key}
Configured nginx site 'rotating-tls' listening on 8443 with ssl_certificate pointing at the rotating cert/key, enabled and started nginx
Verified HTTPS responds 200 on port 8443 using NODE_IP
Created systemd unit cert-renew.service (oneshot running the renewal script) and cert-renew.timer (OnBootSec=1min, OnUnitActiveSec=1min), enabled and started the timer
Ran a 90-second background curl loop against https://$NODE_IP:8443/ spanning a timer-triggered renewal to prove continuous availability

Observed automatic renewal: cert serial changed from 6446C1... to 7B24A6..., journalctl showed nginx config test + reload triggered by the timer, and the loop's aggregated results showed only HTTP 200 responses throughout
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, nginx/timer active status, cert state, HTTPS 200
Issued 'sudo systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled node1 until reachable again

Confirmed changed boot_id and fresh uptime post-reboot, confirmed nginx and cert-renew.timer are active and enabled (persisted across reboot), confirmed the rotated cert persisted on disk, confirmed HTTPS still returns 200
Confirmed cert-renew.timer has a live next-run schedule after reboot

evidence.summary: nginx configured, started, and confirmed serving HTTPS on 8443 with HTTP 200 and correct cert subject/issuer via curl -k

Initial cert issued with 24h validity (serial 6446C1...); systemd timer cert-renew.timer enabled to run every minute; journalctl shows cert-renew.service firing automatically and the cert serial changing to 7B24A6... via the checkend-triggered renewal logic, well before actual expiry

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime)
evidence.summary: A 90-request/1-per-second curl loop against https://$NODE_IP:8443/ spanned the automatic renewal event (nginx -t + systemctl reload triggered by the timer); all 90 responses were HTTP 200, and a follow-up curl confirmed the served cert's expiry now matches the newly renewed cert
Captured boot_id 1e0cb179-..., nginx and cert-renew.timer both active, cert state, and HTTPS 200 before reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo systemctl reboot' returned 'reboot_issued' acknowledgement immediately

evidence.requirement: Node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Connection timed out while node was rebooting, then reconnection succeeded with a new boot_id (9809b0cb-... vs prior 1e0cb179-...) and fresh uptime timestamp, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required services, data, and cluster state
evidence.summary: After reboot, nginx and cert-renew.timer are active and enabled (survived reboot), the rotated certificate persisted on disk unchanged, HTTPS on 8443 returns 200, and the renewal timer has a live next-scheduled run
